rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Its operative provision uses the same distinctive two-part ownership mechanism: federally owned lands within designated exterior boundaries are immediately added and reserved, while state-owned lands become part of the monument upon federal acquisition. Both directives then state that the monument boundaries are modified accordingly. This close language and sequence materially exceed generic national-monument boilerplate. C01 and C04 contain similar machinery, but C17 is the closest verbal and structural match.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following described tracts of land are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Saguaro National Monument; and lands owned by the State of Arizona within such boundaries shall become and be reserved as a part of that monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The lands now owned by the United States within the exterior boundaries of the following-described tracts of land are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Arches National Monument; and lands owned by the State of Utah within such boundaries shall become and be reserved as a part of that monument upon acquisition of title thereto by the United States
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim operative machinery, with only the monument and state names changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The boundaries of the Saguaro National Monument are modified accordingly.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The boundaries of the Arches National Monument are modified accordingly.
